subject: Retention carve-in & DPA amendment for Acme Health — subprocessor routing and purge timeline
messages:
From: Anna Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; procurements@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention carve-in request, subprocessor list & purge timeline

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this. We're moving Acme Health's integration into pilot and legal has a couple of retention-related asks before we sign the amendment:

1) We need a clear statement of your subprocessor routing for backups and logs (where backups are stored, which cloud subprocessor handles nightly snapshots).
2) A backup purge timeline after a data-deletion request (we need a max window and an emergency rollback/escrow option for legal holds).
3) Confirmation of cross-border transfer protections for EU/UK-sourced patient metadata.

Attached: Acme_DPA_Primary.pdf (requested edits in margin) and SFTP-integration-specs.xlsx.

Can your DPA team propose language for an exception that allows a 45-day purge window for backups but with an escrow snapshot retained under legal hold if Acme requests it? Also list practical steps for triggering an emergency hold (who we call internally, typical response SLA).

Appreciate a runbook we can attach to the amendment. We aim to close this week.

Best,
Anna
Anna Gomez
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Health

--
(attachment stubs: Acme_DPA_Primary.pdf, SFTP-integration-specs.xlsx)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Anna Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention carve-in request, subprocessor list & purge timeline

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (privacy counsel) and Karthik (ops) so we can produce a concise amendment + operational runbook.

Summary of proposed approach (high level):
- Subprocessors: primary object storage (AWS S3 us-east-1), snapshot archival (GCS us-east4) — full subprocessor list below and will be included in the DPA annex.
- Backup purge timeline: standard purge occurs 30 days after confirmed deletion request; proposed Acme carve: 45-day purge window to allow for operational reconciliation.
- Legal hold / escrow: during a hold we move a single immutable snapshot (read-only) to an escrow project for 180 days or until the hold is released; access requires combined approvals from Acme legal + Redwood security.
- Emergency hold trigger: Acme can open a request to procurements@redwood.ai or PrivacyOps@redwood.ai; we commit to an initial acknowledgement within 4 business hours and snapshot isolation within 24 hours.

Action items (who does what):
- Kimberly: draft amendment language for DPA carve-in and escrow approval flow (see items 1–3).
- Karthik: prepare a short ops runbook with step-by-step for snapshot isolation, listing responsible on-call roles and expected SLAs. Include evidence capture for audits.
- Laura (me): coordinate DocuSign flow and attach the runbook; confirm timeline with Acme procurement.

I'll prepare a stub amendment for your legal team to review.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

(attachment stubs: redwood-snapshot-policy.pdf)

Subject: Re: Retention carve-in request, subprocessor list & purge timeline

Thanks — I've drafted redlines and some operational constraints. Key points in the draft amendment:

1) Subprocessor disclosure: we will include a named annex listing primary processors (AWS S3 - us-east-1, GCS - us-east4, SFTP partner - FastX SFTP Ltd). We also add a commitment to notify Acme 30 days prior to adding any additional subprocessor that would store backup snapshots.

2) Purge window & escrow: propose the following concrete language — "Redwood will purge backups related to a deletion request within 45 calendar days; however, upon written request from Customer for legal hold, Redwood will isolate a single immutable escrow snapshot within 24 hours and retain it for up to 180 days or until Customer releases the hold."

3) Evidence and auditability: we will provide an audit log export (S3 event manifest + internal ops ticket ID) proving snapshot isolation and subsequent purge. We attach a template evidence package.

Operational caveat from Karthik (below) — we may need an SLA exception for extremely large accounts where snapshoting takes longer than 24h; propose an upper-bound clause: "typical isolation within 24h; for volumes >100TB, isolation target is 72h with status updates every 8h."

Questions for Acme legal: is 180 days acceptable for escrow? If you need longer we can discuss staged extensions with extra contractual guardrails.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Laura / Kimberly / Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and useful language. Acme legal reviewed the amendment and has the following confirmations:

- 45-day purge window is acceptable for this pilot.
- 180-day escrow snapshot retention is acceptable, provided Redwood documents the access approvals and provides the audit manifest upon purge.
- The upper-bound SLA for very large volumes (72h) is acceptable as long as we receive 8h status updates during the isolation window.

Procurement will proceed with the DocuSign amendment. Please attach the ops runbook and the evidence template.

Next steps:
- Laura: please upload the runbook to the shared drive link and send the DocuSign package to procurements@acmehealth.com.
- Kimberly: include the notification clause for new backup subprocessors and the 30-day prior notice commitment.

We appreciate the clarity — looking forward to getting to pilot.

Anna Gomez

Acme Health
